7: - [x] 1.5 In the handler, constructor-inject `IEmailVerificationTokenValidator` (non-nullable). The verification step MUST run before any event/catalog/coupon load. If `EmailVerificationToken is null` → reject with `email.verification_required` *without* calling the validator. Otherwise call the validator; a `false` result maps to `email.verification_invalid`. (In this change, calling the validator with a non-null token will throw `NotImplementedException` from the placeholder; that is intentional — see D7.)
8: - [x] 1.6 Centralize all error constants on `RegisterAttendeeHandler.Errors` with the same codes as today (`registration.event_not_found`, `registration.event_not_active`, `registration.not_open`, `registration.closed`, `registration.email_domain_not_allowed`, `registration.no_ticket_types`, `registration.duplicate_ticket_types`, `registration.unknown_ticket_types`, `registration.cancelled_ticket_types`, `registration.overlapping_time_slots`, `coupon.not_found`, `coupon.expired`, `coupon.already_redeemed`, `coupon.revoked`, `coupon.ticket_type_not_allowed`) plus three new codes: `email.verification_required`, `email.verification_invalid`, `coupon.email_mismatch`.

The fixture MUST inject a fake `IEmailVerificationTokenValidator` into the test container (overriding the production placeholder), defaulting to a stub that succeeds when `token == "VALID-TOKEN-FOR-{email}"` so tests are self-explanatory.
25: - [x] 3.2 Create `RegisterAttendeeHandlerTests` covering all scenarios from `SelfRegisterAttendeeTests`, `AdminRegisterAttendeeTests`, and `RegisterWithCouponTests`. Use `[Theory]` over `RegistrationMode` for shared assertions (active-gate, ticket-type validation, additional-details validation, claim safety net) and `[Fact]` for mode-specific behavior. Preserve every `SC###`-prefixed scenario name.
26: - [x] 3.3 Add new handler tests for the verification scenarios from the modified `attendee-registration` spec: token-missing → `email.verification_required`; token-invalid → `email.verification_invalid`; verification runs before any other lookup (assert by setting up a non-existent event id and confirming the verification error is returned).

2: name: cli-api-client-generation
3: description: Refresh the Admitto CLI NSwag ApiClient through the approved Aspire-backed generation workflow.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Skill: cli-api-client-generation
7: 
8: ## Purpose
9: 
10: Update the Admitto CLI generated API client through the approved workflow whenever backend endpoint changes affect `src/Admitto.Cli/Api/ApiClient.g.cs`.
11: 
12: ## Use when
13: 
14: - backend endpoint additions, removals, or signature changes affect the CLI API surface
15: - `src/Admitto.Cli/Api/ApiClient.g.cs` must be refreshed
16: - a CLI command depends on newly generated client methods
17: 
18: ## Inputs
19: 
20: - the changed backend endpoint surface
21: - the CLI project at `src/Admitto.Cli`
22: - the generation script at `src/Admitto.Cli/generate-api-client.sh`
23: - the existing Aspire AppHost configuration
24: 
25: ## Required workflow
26: 
27: 1. Use the `aspire` skill to start or refresh the AppHost.
28: 2. Wait for the API and other relevant resources to become healthy.
29: 3. Confirm the backend surface needed for OpenAPI generation is available.
30: 4. Run [`src/Admitto.Cli/generate-api-client.sh`](/Users/REDACTED_USER/Code/amolenk/Admitto/src/Admitto.Cli/generate-api-client.sh).
31: 5. Review the generated client diff.
32: 6. Build the CLI project.
33: 7. Inspect Aspire resource health before declaring the generation pass complete.
34: 
35: ## Must validate
36: 
37: - `ApiClient.g.cs` changed only through the generation script
38: - the generated client matches the current backend contract
39: - the CLI project compiles after regeneration
40: - relevant Aspire resources are healthy
41: 
42: ## Must not do
43: 
44: - edit `src/Admitto.Cli/Api/ApiClient.g.cs` manually
45: - bypass the generation script with ad hoc manual code changes
46: - assume the API is healthy without checking Aspire resource status
47: - finish the workflow without a CLI build
48: 
49: ## Outputs
50: 
51: - updated generated CLI client produced by `generate-api-client.sh`
52: - a brief record that Aspire was started or refreshed and resources were checked
53: - a note for reviewers when no client regeneration was required
54: 
55: ## Override points
56: 
57: - the exact Aspire resource names to wait for
58: - any additional CLI verification command beyond the basic build
59: 
60: ## Examples
61: 
62: - Regenerating the CLI client after adding a new admin endpoint.
63: - Refreshing generated methods after a request or response contract change.
